group_assessment.weighting: A paediatric nutrition and neurology group at Ain Shams University, Cairo (from the affiliations) reporting a single-centre open trial of 30 children; descriptive/interventional clinical. Not a WWOX group; SUBSTITUTE for the carnitine axis (class level, not WWOX evidence). The tables and the Results text are weighed above the abstract and conclusion framing, where several claims outrun the tests.

entries.proposition: NOT WWOX EVIDENCE (substitute, carnitine axis). The primary endpoint is a within-arm change: antral length rose significantly in the carnitine arm (P = 0.039) and showed no significant difference in the diet-only arm (P = 0.925), and the results report no between-arm test of antral length even though the abstract frames it as a comparison with the non-supplemented group.
entries.snippet: On the other hand, there was no significant difference regarding antral length in the patients who only received KD upon follow up (P-value 0.925).

entries.proposition: The between-arm comparison of GI symptom score and Bristol stool scale did not reach significance; only defecation frequency did (50 percent rise in the carnitine arm, 33 percent fall in the diet-only arm).
entries.snippet: Although there was a decrease in the median (IQR) of GI symptoms score in the patients on KD with L-carnitine supplementation in comparison to KD only group indicating clinical improvement in GI symptoms, and an increase in the median (IQR) of the Bristol stool scale indicating that the stool was softer, these results didn’t reach statistical significance.
